deep.reconstruction:
This page is the continuation of §1 of a draft, and §2, of what appears to be Ramanujan's paper 'A series for Euler's constant γ' (Messenger of Math. 46 (1917), 73–80). The general formula of §1 is on the preceding page, which is not in the context given. From the three special cases I reconstruct it as follows; this reconstruction is mine.

General formula (§1, inferred): for b>1 and a>0 (with c + a/b > 0),
  ∫_0^1 ( x^{c-1}/(1-x) − b·x^{bc-1}/(1-x^b) ) · Σ_{k≥0} x^{a b^k} dx = ψ(c + a/b) + log(b/a).

Derivation (mine):
- Use ∫_0^1 ( x^{s-1}/(1-x) + 1/log x ) dx = −ψ(s).
- Substituting y = x^b gives ∫_0^1 ( b·x^{bs-1}/(1-x^b) + x^{b-1}/log x ) dx = −ψ(s).
- By (10), ∫_0^1 (1 − x^{b-1})/log x dx = log b.
- So the k-th term equals ψ(ab^{k-1}+c) − ψ(ab^k+c) + log b.
- Summing k = 0..N telescopes to ψ(a/b+c) − ψ(ab^N+c) + (N+1)·log b.
- Since ψ(ab^N+c) = log a + N·log b + o(1), the limit is ψ(c+a/b) + log(b/a).

When a = b and c = 1 the right side is ψ(2) = 1 − γ. Simplifying the kernel gives the three cases on the page:
- (7) a=b=2, c=1. The kernel 1/(1−x) − 2x/(1−x²) equals 1/(1+x). Hence 1−γ = ∫_0^1 (x²+x⁴+x⁸+…)/(1+x) dx.
- (8) a=b=3, c=1. The kernel 1/(1−x) − 3x²/(1−x³) = (1−x)(1+2x)/(1−x³) = (1+2x)/(1+x+x²). Hence 1−γ = ∫_0^1 (1+2x)/(1+x+x²) · (x³+x⁹+x²⁷+…) dx.
- (9) a=b=3/2, c=1. Put t = √x. The kernel 1/(1−t²) − (3/2)t/(1−t³) has numerator 1 − t/2 − t²/2 = (1−t)(1+t/2). It reduces to (1+½√x)/((1+√x)(1+√x+x)). Hence 1−γ = ∫_0^1 that kernel · (x^{3/2} + x^{(3/2)²} + …) dx.

As a cross-check, (7) is equivalent to Catalan's integral. Write x^{2^n}/(1+x) = x^{2^n−1} − x^{2^n−1}/(1+x). Summing gives Σ 2^{-n} − γ = 1 − γ.

§2. Start from the Frullani-type integral (10): ∫_0^1 (x^{p-1} − x^{q-1})/log x dx = log(q/p), for p, q > 0.
- Take p = ab^k + c and q = ab^k + bc.
- Then term k of (11) equals log((ab^k+bc)/(ab^k+c)) = log( b·(ab^{k-1}+c)/(ab^k+c) ).
- The partial product over k = 0..N is b^{N+1}·(a/b+c)/(ab^N+c). This tends to b(a/b+c)/a = 1 + bc/a.
- This gives (11): ∫_0^1 (x^{c-1} − x^{bc-1})/log x · Σ_{k≥0} x^{ab^k} dx = log(1 + bc/a).
- Ramanujan's stated conditions are b > 1, a+c > 0 and a+bc > 0.

The heading '3.' is left blank.
errors: (11): the stated conditions (b>1, a+c>0, a+bc>0) are not sufficient on their own; a>0 is also needed. If a<0 then ab^k+c becomes negative for large k, and if a=0 the series diverges. With a>0 the stated conditions suffice: ab^k+c ≥ a+c > 0 and ab^k+bc = b(ab^{k-1}+c) > 0 ⇔ a+bc > 0. The tacit assumption a>0 is presumably made in the general setup on the previous page.

In (7)–(9) the interchange of sum and integral, and the telescoping of individually divergent pieces, need the 1/log x regularization (or an equivalent device). The final results are nevertheless correct; I verified each kernel simplification and the values ψ(2) = 1 − γ.

results.modern_name: Catalan's integral for γ (dyadic; equivalent to Vacca's series)
results.usually_credited_to: E. Catalan (1875); series form G. Vacca (1910)

results.what: Base-b generalization: ∫_0^1 (x^{c-1}/(1−x) − b x^{bc-1}/(1−x^b)) Σ x^{ab^k} dx = ψ(c+a/b) + log(b/a), with the cases a=b=3 and a=b=3/2 giving 1−γ (general form inferred)
results.modern_name: Generalized Catalan/Vacca integrals for Euler's constant (base-b digit-type representations)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (1917 Messenger paper); later base-b series by Addison (1967) and others

results.what: ∫_0^1 (x^{c-1} − x^{bc-1})/log x · Σ x^{ab^k} dx = log(1 + bc/a)
results.modern_name: Telescoping lacunary-series application of the Frullani-type integral ∫_0^1 (x^{p-1}−x^{q-1})/log x dx = log(q/p)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan, 'A series for Euler's constant γ' (1917)

deep.surprise_reason: This page appears to be a manuscript draft of material published in Ramanujan's 1917 Messenger paper on Vacca-type series for γ. The results are known and already attributed to him; (7) is Catalan's classical integral.

checkable.asserts: the kernel for a=b=3, c=1 simplifies to (1+2x)/(1+x+x²) (result 0)
the kernel for a=b=3/2, c=1 with t=√x matches (9) (result 0)
(11) with a=3, b=2, c=1 gives log(1+bc/a) = log(5/3)
the telescoping product in (11) for a=3, b=2, c=1 tends to 1+bc/a

transcription_corrections: The pencil marginal notes 'a=b=2, c=1', 'a=b=3, c=1' and 'a=b=1½, c=1' are faint annotations in the right margin, possibly in a later hand. They are not part of the displayed equations.
In (9) the exponents are x^{1½}, x^{(1½)²}, x^{(1½)³}, i.e. x^{(3/2)^k} for k ≥ 1; the transcription is correct.
The header reads 'Add. Ms a 94 18(25)' with folio number 25 circled.
